title: The Cabin Inn and the Sissy Club on State Street
summary: Her husband describes managing the Cabin Inn, its origins as the Sissy Club with female impersonators, its moves and owners, and radio links.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

Did it start off early in its history as the Sissy Club because it developed a reputation?

Well, no. I'll tell you what happened. The Sissy Club in the Cabin Inn was in the 34th block that came from 31st Street in Cottage Grove. Big Ivy who was passed on and another guy named Jack what was Jack's name? I forget his name now. But they started off with the Cabin Inn and they were using female impersonators. So the place got too small at 31st Cottage and they moved in the 34th block on State Street.

And they had a tremendous business there. Pretty big place too. I forget the address there. I think it was 34, 34, 35 or something. 34, 30. right across from the old Mecca building. So then they closed there and then Big Ivy opened the Dream Land. And then after that he closed then his son opened up and still called it the Cabin Inn.
